newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil civil service reform voting delayed again.
newsitem.headline: Brazil civil service reform voting delayed again.

text.p: Voting on outstanding amendments to the Brazilian government's civil service reform bill has been delayed yet again, this time because of a reshuffle among whips in the Chamber of Deputies, a congressional official said.
"It was decided that we should let things settle a little. Reshuffles are always a little traumatic," said a spokeswoman for the government-allied Liberal Front Party (PFL).
The spokeswoman said leaders of several government-allied parties decided at a meeting earlier Wednesday they would try to resume the drawn out process of voting on the amendments next week.

The Chamber of Deputies approved the text of the civil service reform two months ago but the government, hampered by internal party wrangling and an alleged corruption scandal, has struggled to muster support to kill opposition amendments.
After failing to defeat an amendment which removed a key article of the bill, government whips preferred to stall voting with delaying tactics on the floor of the lower house.
About 20 amendments have yet to be voted on, but only four are considered as potentially damaging to the reform, including one which seeks to maintain the right of civil servants to a job for life.

The government's hopes of making progress on the reform looked likely to rest with Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes who is expected to announce later Wednesday that he will accept the job of chief whip in the Chamber of Deputies.

Magalhaes helped the government approve several important reforms while president of the lower house between 1995 and earlier this year and he is considered one of the most dynamic figures in Congress.
Reports that he had been offered the job by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso ruffled the feathers of Benito Gama, who Tuesday resigned acrimoniously as chief whip.
